Description: A theme-aware web component that holds the host's content in a window, under a taskbar that brings the window's controls. The panel is part of the page's HTML when the page loads, and the host defines the five controls, then `task-bar`, then `window-panel`, each after loading its template.

template.description: The HTML template for the panel component.

div.window.description: The surface of the window. It holds the taskbar along its top and the content below it.

task-bar.description: The taskbar of the panel: the `task-bar` component, which brings the pin and the minimize, maximize, restore and close controls. The host defines the five controls, then `task-bar`, and loads their templates, before the panel. Cached as `elements.taskbar`: the panel listens to each control through it, with the control's own `on…` properties, so that connecting the panel again never subscribes twice, and hides the controls that do not fit its `condition`. The pin's `onpin` leads to the panel's `pin`, and its `onunpin` to `unpin`: the end user pins and unpins the panel by clicking the pin. The minimize control's `onminimize` leads to the panel's `minimize`, the maximize control's `onmaximize` to `maximize`, the restore control's `onrestore` to `restore`, and the close control's `onclose` to `close`. The taskbar removes nothing itself: closing is the panel's.

slot.title.description: The place where the title the host gives the panel is shown, in the centre of the taskbar. The host marks the title with `slot="title"`. The title is the host's own: the panel neither listens to it nor changes it.

div.content.description: The region below the taskbar. It holds the slot for the host's content. It is not shown while the panel is `minimized`.

slot.description: The place where the content the host places inside the panel is shown. The content is the host's own: the panel neither listens to it nor changes it.

condition.description: Indicates whether the window is normal, collapsed to its taskbar, or enlarged to fill the space it has. While `minimized`, only the taskbar is shown, where the panel sits; the panel keeps the position and the dimensions it had. While `maximized`, the panel fills the space it has, which is the element it is positioned in; it also keeps the position and the dimensions it had. It decides which controls the taskbar shows: minimize and maximize while `normal`; restore and maximize while `minimized`; minimize and restore while `maximized`. Close is always shown. The pin is hidden while `maximized`, and shown otherwise, with the `status` the panel holds.

status.description: Indicates whether the window is pinned in place or unpinned. The panel holds it, and the pin in the taskbar shows it.

visibility.description: Indicates whether the panel is visible or hidden. A hidden panel is not shown and keeps everything else as it is: when it is shown again, it is as it was.

position.description: Where the panel is: the place of its upper left corner in the element it is positioned in. It is `null` until the panel is moved or given a position; until then the panel is where the host application placed it. A `minimized` panel has and keeps a position; a `maximized` panel keeps its position without showing it.

left.description: The distance from the left edge of the element the panel is positioned in, in pixels.

top.description: The distance from the top edge of the element the panel is positioned in, in pixels.

hide.description: Sets `visibility` to `hidden` and hides the panel.

show.description: Sets `visibility` to `visible` and shows the panel.

pin.description: Sets `status` to `pinned`, and the pin in the taskbar shows pinned.

unpin.description: Sets `status` to `unpinned`, and the pin in the taskbar shows unpinned.

minimize.description: Sets `condition` to `minimized`, and collapses the panel to its taskbar.

maximize.description: Sets `condition` to `maximized`, and enlarges the panel to fill the space it has.

restore.description: Returns the panel to how it was. A `maximized` panel becomes `normal`. A `minimized` panel returns to the `condition` it had when it was minimized, `normal` or `maximized`; a panel that was `minimized` from the start becomes `normal`. A `normal` panel stays as it is.

close.description: Closes the panel: dispatches `onclose`, then removes the panel from the page. A panel that is not in the page stays as it is, and nothing is dispatched.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Contains the new visibility of the panel.

parameters.description: Contains the new status of the panel.

onminimize.description: Dispatched when `condition` changes from `normal` or `maximized` to `minimized`.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Contains the new condition of the panel.

onmaximize.description: Dispatched when `condition` changes from `normal` or `minimized` to `maximized`.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Contains the new condition of the panel.

onrestore.description: Dispatched when `condition` changes from `minimized` or `maximized` to `normal`.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Contains the new condition of the panel.

onclose.description: Dispatched each time the panel closes, before it is removed from the page. It replaces the `onclose` property every HTML element has.

onmove.description: Dispatched each time the end user drags the panel to a new position: once for every step of the drag.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.description: Contains the new position of the panel.

pointerdown.description: User presses on the taskbar to start dragging the panel.

triggers.condition: the panel is `unpinned` and not `maximized`, and the press is not on a control of the taskbar

pointermove.description: User moves the pointer while dragging: the panel follows it.

pointerup.description: User lifts the pointer: the drag ends where the panel is.

pointercancel.description: The browser ends the press, such as when a touch is taken over: the drag ends where the panel is.
